title: Analog quantum simulation of bosonic and anyonic models with flux-driven transmons
authors: Isak Lyngfelt, Jorge Fernández-Pendás, Göran Johansson, Laura Garciá-Álvarez
abstract: When quantum particles interact, many-body phenomena that are hard to simulate classically emerge. Quantum analog simulation offers an alternative in which the target system's dynamics is directly realized in controllable quantum hardware. Here, we give a general protocol for simulating the Bose-Hubbard and anyon-Hubbard models using lattices of capacitively coupled flux-tunable transmons. By modulating the transmon frequencies in an alternating pattern, we resonantly drive multiple many-body transitions and can tune the on-site interaction and density-dependent hopping amplitudes for up to three bosons per site, with no additional restriction on the total particle number. By adding phases to the modulation, which renders the transition amplitudes complex-valued, we propose the first simulation protocol for the anyon-Hubbard model with transmons. Numerical simulations of the driven transmon arrays with experimentally realistic parameters reproduce the characteristic dynamics of the target models across a range of interaction strengths and statistical phases, including the interaction-dependent localization and the statistics-dependent asymmetry of the anyonic quantum walk.
summary: This paper details a general protocol to simulate interacting bosonic and anyonic lattice models using superconducting transmon arrays. By precisely modulating the transmon frequencies, the authors can engineer the necessary on-site interactions and hopping terms for both the Bose-Hubbard and Anyon-Hubbard models. This work is significant because it demonstrates a scalable, controllable platform for studying strongly correlated quantum matter beyond current simulation limits.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating complex many-body phenomena, specifically bosonic and anyonic interactions, which are difficult to model using classical computational methods.
main_result: The authors propose a general, tunable protocol using superconducting transmon arrays to realize the dynamics of both the Bose-Hubbard and Anyon-Hubbard models.
method: The simulation is achieved by resonantly driving the frequencies of capacitively coupled transmons in an alternating pattern, which effectively engineers the required interaction and hopping terms.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a lattice of flux-tunable transmons. The target models are the Bose-Hubbard (BH) model and the Anyon-Hubbard (AH) model, which describe interacting bosons/anyons on a lattice.
key_observables: Interaction-dependent localization and the statistics-dependent asymmetry of the anyonic quantum walk.
important_parameters: On-site interaction strength (U), hopping amplitude (J), and the statistical phase ($	heta$) for anyons.
main_assumptions: The protocol relies on resonant driving and uses approximations like the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA) and a first-order Fourier expansion for the time-dependent frequency modulation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum walk dynamics for the BH model across varying interaction strengths and show the total leakage probability in the AH model as a function of interaction strength.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of simulating interacting quantum systems, details the general protocol using transmon arrays to map the BH and AH Hamiltonians, presents numerical results demonstrating the capability to tune parameters and observe characteristic dynamics, and discusses limitations like leakage.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, hardware-agnostic blueprint for simulating fundamental models of strongly correlated matter (like the Hubbard model) using superconducting circuits, bridging theoretical condensed matter physics with quantum hardware realization.

FIG. 4. A quantum walk of two particles initialized in each of sites one and twelve in a 4 × 3 grid for U = {0, 3J, 10J}. For each interaction strength, the left plot shows the exact dynamics of the BH model, Eq. (2), and the right plot, the simulated transmon system. The system contains four particles, which exceeds the maximum occupation per site, Nmax = 3, so the truncation is not guaranteed by particle-number conservation.

FIG. 5. A quantum walk of a triplon initialized at site six in a ten site 1D chain for U = {0, 2J, 4J}. For each interaction strength, the left plot shows the exact dynamics of the BH model, Eq. (2), and the right plot, the simulated transmon system.

FIG. 6. A quantum walk for two interacting anyons initialized on the same site for U = 0 and U = 2J in the top and bottom row respectively. For each interaction strength, the left plot shows the exact dynamics of the AH model, Eq. (3), the right plot is the simulated transmon system. We consider the statistical phases θ = π/4, π/2 and 3π/4 for both interaction strengths in the left, middle and right plots respectively. For the non-interacting system, the state delocalizes as the phase increases. For the interacting system, the quantum walk is asymmetric.
